title: Perfect Acceptance Characterizes Dictators
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f$ map the sign cube $\\{-1,1\\}^n$ to $\\{-1,1\\}$. The tester that chooses uniformly between the odd BLR equation test and the sign-AND test accepts $f$ with probability one if and only if $f$ is a dictator; that is, there is a coordinate $i\\in[n]$ such that $f(x)=x_i$ for every $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
